comments.body:
Census complete against a fresh `origin/main` worktree at `71a719aef88`. Counts reproduced exactly: **51 total failures, 4 SemLock (excluded, `0eba`), 47 in scope.** No nondeterminism — the population is stable.

## Verdict on the ticket's final criterion

**`make verify` can be made green under the sandbox. There is no irreducible residue.** All 47, plus the 4 SemLock failures, are addressable while preserving full CI coverage, using direct capability probes and loud counted local signals.

## Distinct root causes: 5

| Cause | Count |
|---|---:|
| Injected Git command-line identity overrides test-local identity | 20 |
| Wrong-architecture / missing pandoc host binary | 17 |
| Sandboxed home breaks semgrep fallback | 8 |
| Sandbox denies `ps` | 1 |
| Baseline close-gate branch/ref mismatch | 1 |

Every attribution is **probe-confirmed**. None were inferred from traceback alone.

## The reframing: only one of five is actually a sandbox denial

This is the finding that matters most, and it contradicts the ticket's own framing — which I wrote, assuming these were sandbox capability denials like the SemLock four.

- **`ps` (1)** is the only genuine sandbox syscall denial. `ps -A -o pid=,ppid=,time=,command=` raises `PermissionError errno=1`.

- **Git identity (20)** is a **harness artifact, not a sandbox restriction**. The harness injects `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT=8` with command-line `user.name=Joe Oakhart` / `user.email=joeoakhart@navapbc.com`. Command-line config outranks both repo-local config and a fake `HOME`, so identity-sensitive tests cannot isolate themselves — and tests asserting that a *missing* email aborts instead find one. Removing those `GIT_CONFIG_*` variables makes **28 targeted identity tests pass**. This is the largest single cause and the cheapest to fix.

- **pandoc (17)** is not a sandbox issue at all. The bundled `pypandoc` binary is **`Mach-O 64-bit executable x86_64` on an `arm64` host**; executing it raises `OSError: [Errno 86] Bad CPU type in executable`, and no system pandoc is on `PATH`. **This would break for any Apple Silicon developer**, sandboxed or not. It is a dependency packaging defect that the sandbox merely exposed. One test compounds it by then trying `""` and getting `PermissionError: [Errno 13] Permission denied: ''`.

- **semgrep (8)** is a test-harness environment assumption. `opengrep` is absent; the `semgrep` fallback exists but fails opening the real-home `/Users/joeoakhart/.semgrep/settings.yml` under sandbox EPERM, so detectors abstain and advisory notes read `fail-open-abstain` rather than `detector-finding`. Redirecting `HOME` into worktree scratch makes all 8 pass. Note the deeper issue: availability is tested by `shutil.which`, which reports a binary that cannot actually run.

- **Close-gate (1)** is an **ordinary baseline bug with no environmental component** — see below.

## A real defect found incidentally

`tests/interfaces/lifecycle/test_completion_gate.py::test_file_impact_close_fetches_before_rejecting_stale_clone` fails for reasons unrelated to the sandbox. The copied fixture repo is on `master` while the remote commit is on `origin/main`, and `commit_impact.upstream_branch_refs()` only includes refs ending in `/<current-branch>` — so the include-upstream scan ignores `origin/main` even after a successful fetch.

That is a genuine bug in the completion gate's stale-clone handling, not a test artifact, and it is being filed separately. It is adjacent to `8806`, which also concerns the completion gate verifying against the wrong tree.

## Remediation per cause

- **Git identity:** scrub inherited `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` command-line overrides in identity-sensitive tests, or resolve identity through a properly isolated environment. Largest win, smallest change.
- **pandoc:** provide an architecture-correct dependency, or probe by **direct execution** rather than `shutil.which`, with loud counted local unavailability and unchanged CI execution. The packaging defect should be fixed regardless, since it affects arm64 developers generally.
- **semgrep:** run semgrep/opengrep out-of-process with sandboxed `HOME` and tool state, and redefine availability as "can execute a trivial scan" rather than "binary is on `PATH`".
- **`ps`:** the only case needing the probe-and-loud-signal treatment. Preserve CI coverage; emit a counted local signal when a direct `ps` probe fails.
- **Close-gate:** fix as an ordinary bug on its own ticket.

All three hard constraints are satisfiable: CI coverage unchanged, no silent skips, and every detection above is a direct capability probe rather than an environment-name heuristic.

Full traceback log: `.rebar/scratch/1352ecab-4910-4535-9368-1dc8a0029977-20590/make-test.log` in the investigation worktree.

No fixes were implemented, no tracker writes were made, and no push occurred.

compiled_state.description:
## Status: remediation, scope narrowed after plan review

The census this ticket originally planned is complete and recorded in the comments. Plan review then established that the pandoc population does not belong here, so it has been split to `dc28-2807-5b1d-4da7`. This ticket now covers **29** failures across **3** causes.

## Established findings

`make test` under the agent sandbox on unmodified `origin/main` fails **51** tests, reproducibly, with no nondeterminism across repeated runs. The split:

| Cause | Count | Mechanism | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Git identity | 20 | The harness exports command-scope `GIT_CONFIG_COUNT` / `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_n` / `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_n`, which every inherited-environment git subprocess honors over repo-local config | **This ticket** |
| semgrep | 8 | Writing the real-home `~/.semgrep/settings.yml` is denied | **This ticket** |
| `ps` | 1 | Process enumeration denied — the only genuine sandbox denial | **This ticket** |
| pandoc | 17 | Bundled `pypandoc` binary is x86_64 on arm64 | `dc28-2807-5b1d-4da7` |
| SemLock | 4 | Darwin `sem_open` denied with `EPERM` | `0eba-cfd8-34b0-4cb7` |
| Close gate | 1 | Ordinary baseline defect, unrelated to environment | `9753-647b-2f85-40ef` |

**Worker count is not a remedy for any part of this.** The runner-level (pytest-xdist) failure population measured exactly **0**; xdist brings its pool up successfully and reaches 99% of the suite. `PYTEST_WORKERS=1` does not bypass xdist at all, since `make test` hardcodes `-n $(PYTEST_WORKERS)`.

**Attribution at verification time.** Each of the 29 failures is enumerated by pytest nodeid in the census comment on this ticket, grouped by cause. Verification checks those named nodeids individually rather than inferring a cause from a residual count, so a newly-introduced failure cannot be mistaken for a fixed one.

## Approach

### 1. Git identity (20) — consolidate the existing helper, do not write a second one

A scrub for exactly this already exists: `scrub_ambient_git_config()` in `tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py:26`, covering the same four prefixes (`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, `GIT_CONFIG_KEY_`, `GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_`, `GIT_CONFIG_PARAMETERS`), called at lines 41 and 143, with a docstring naming the same harness cause.

Writing a second copy in `tests/conftest.py` would duplicate a mechanism and invite the two to drift — and a duplicated `test_helper` is itself what the mechanism-delta ratchet flags. Instead: **lift `scrub_ambient_git_config` and its `_GIT_CONFIG_INJECTION_PREFIXES` into a shared `tests/` helper module**, and have both the existing bridge call sites and the new conftest fixture import the one implementation. Net mechanism count does not increase.

Population note: 20 is the count of currently **failing** tests attributable to this cause. Removing the injected variables makes 28 identity tests pass, a superset that includes 8 which already pass and must continue to. The acceptance criteria below are stated against the failing population of 20.

### 2. semgrep (8)

Redirect the settings path to a per-run scratch location so the real home is never written. Measured: all 8 pass under a redirected `HOME`. Prefer semgrep's own settings-path variable over redirecting `HOME` wholesale, since a blanket `HOME` redirect silently changes behaviour for anything else in the process that reads it.

### 3. `ps` (1)

No remedy exists; enumeration is denied outright. This is the single test that legitimately cannot run, and it takes a counted skip.

### 4. Skip accounting under xdist — controller-side aggregation

The counted-skip signal is the property this ticket exists to enforce, and a naive session-scoped counter **does not deliver it**: under xdist each worker is a separate process, so a per-worker counter reports fragments or zero rather than a suite total, and the no-silent-skips guarantee fails exactly where it is needed.

Aggregate on the controller: workers publish their counts through the xdist `workeroutput` mechanism, and the controller sums them in `pytest_terminal_summary`. The accounting test must run **with xdist enabled**, because a test that only passes single-process would not exercise the failure mode.

### Constraints

- **Capability probes only, never environment-name heuristics.** Detection attempts the operation and observes the outcome. Username, hostname, and CI variables are not acceptable discriminators. A probe is also what keeps this portable: it behaves correctly under any CI provider and under none.
- **No CI coverage may be lost.** Probes resolve to available in CI, so the skip paths are unreachable there.
- Any genuinely new mechanism carries a `# mechanism-ok:` marker at its definition site naming this ticket. The baseline is not hand-edited.

## Testing strategy

TDD throughout: each cause gets a failing test written first, then the fix.

- Probe correctness is tested against a **stub** that simulates the denied capability, not against the ambient environment, so the tests assert the same thing on a host that has the capability and one that does not.
- Each probe gets a positive-path test proving it reports "available" when the capability works, so a probe hardcoded to "unavailable" — which would silently disable tests in CI — fails the suite.
- The skip accounting is tested under xdist, asserting the controller's summary reports the suite total.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The 20 git-identity nodeids enumerated in the census comment pass under the agent sandbox. Verified by `pytest` on those nodeids exiting 0.
- [ ] The 8 semgrep nodeids enumerated in the census comment pass under the agent sandbox. Verified by `pytest` on those nodeids exiting 0.
- [ ] The 1 `ps` nodeid skips under the agent sandbox rather than failing. Verified by `pytest` on that nodeid exiting 0 with a reported skip.
- [ ] Exactly one implementation of the git-config scrub exists in the tree. Verified by `[ "$(grep -rc 'GIT_CONFIG_INJECTION_PREFIXES' tests/ --include=*.py | grep -cv ':0$')" -eq 1 ]`.
- [ ] `tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py` imports the scrub from the shared helper rather than defining it. Verified by `grep -q '^def scrub_ambient_git_config' tests/scripts/test_run_reconcile_bridge.py` returning non-zero.
- [ ] A test asserts each probe reports "unavailable" against a stub simulating denial. Verified by that test passing on a host where the capability works.
- [ ] A test asserts each probe reports "available" when the capability works. Verified by that test failing when the probe is stubbed to return a constant "unavailable".
- [ ] The skip counter reports the suite total when running under xdist with more than one worker. Verified by an accounting test run with `-n 2` asserting the summary count equals the number of skipped capabilities.
- [ ] No hostname, username, or CI environment variable appears in the remedy. Verified by `! git diff origin/main -- tests/ | grep -E '^\+.*(GITHUB_|CI=|hostname|getuser)'`.
- [ ] `make test` in CI collects the same test count as `origin/main`. Verified by comparing the collected count in the CI log against a baseline run.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_mechanism_delta.py --check` reports 0 new unadmitted mechanisms. Verified by that command exiting 0.
- [ ] `make test` under the agent sandbox reports 22 failures, down from 51. Verified by running `make test` under the sandbox and counting.

## Out of scope

pandoc (`dc28-2807-5b1d-4da7`). SemLock (`0eba-cfd8-34b0-4cb7`). The close-gate defect (`9753-647b-2f85-40ef`). Whether `make verify` reaches exit 0 overall is contingent on those siblings landing and is not verifiable from this ticket alone.
